sections.title: Whole-Column Hydraulic Compression
body: PC08 solves bed compression differently than every other ECOM line. Instead of an internal piston moving inside a fixed tube, the hydraulics sit in the stand itself, and the whole column gets pressed upward against a fixed flange at the top of the system.

For the 150 and 200 millimeter columns, that pressing continues actively during use. A 40 ton hydraulic cylinder, double action with a 200 to 600 millimeter stroke, compensates for bed volume changes as separation runs, rather than only packing once at the start. The stand connects to the upper flange through five rods, robust enough to hold the whole assembly under that force, while still letting the column itself come out without taking the frame apart.

The letter after the model name tells you the cylinder type, D for double-action, or S for a spring-return cylinder typically used on smaller systems. The two-letter code that follows covers the pump and gauge together: MM means a manual pump paired with a mechanical manometer, while EE means a motor-driven pump paired with an electronic pressure gauge. Smaller single-action cylinders rely on liquid pressure to retract the piston, since they can't pull it out mechanically on their own. Once you move into D30 and above, motor-driven pumps become the only option, simply because the oil-flow rate needed at that scale isn't practical to generate by hand.
